Floor Chute Trap.name: Floor Chute Trap
Floor Chute Trap.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:22] (trained) to prevent the floor from pivoting
Floor Chute Trap.hazarddescription: A pivoted section of a seemingly normal hallway becomes a chute that deposits victims into a more dangerous room.
Floor Chute Trap.reset: Provided no creature is on the slide, the trap resets after 1 minute, returning the hallway floor to its normal, unassuming state.

Look Out Below.name: Look Out Below
Look Out Below.description:
Trigger A creature attempts to open the door at the end of the hallway

Effect The section of floor marked on the map drops down, becoming a steep ramp. Creatures in the easternmost square fall 5 feet, creatures in the middle square fall 10 feet, and creatures in the western square fall 15 feet (DC 21 to [[/act grab-an-edge dc=21]]). In that order, all creatures who fall are moved to one of the squares immediately east of the marked squares in area A11. If any destination square is occupied, the creature in that square is pushed 5 feet to the east as the second creature takes its place, and both creatures take an additional @Damage[2d6[bludgeoning]|traits:nonlethal]{2d6 nonlethal bludgeoning damage} (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic] save).

Trial by Flame Trap.name: Trial by Flame Trap
Trial by Flame Trap.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:23] (trained) to disable the nozzles or @Check[arcana|dc:26] (expert) or @Check[occultism|dc:26] (expert) to disable the nearby magical sensor
Trial by Flame Trap.hazarddescription: Nozzles connected to reservoirs of alchemist's fire are hidden just under the packed dirt of the floor, ready to spew burning jets when deployed.
Trial by Flame Trap.reset: The trap resets when an operator at the maze console in area A13 pulls the associated lever. The trap can be reset only once per minute.

Burning Jets.name: Burning Jets
Burning Jets.description:
Trigger An operator at the maze console in area A13 pulls the associated lever

Effect Three hidden nozzles rise from the ground, and each makes a flame jet Strike against a creature in the area marked on the map. A creature can be hit more than once if there are fewer than three targets. On a critical hit, the target takes 1d10 persistent fire damage.

Sticky Toffee Hound.name: Sticky Toffee Hound
Sticky Toffee Hound.publicNotes:
Sweet hags have an affinity for baking and take delight in corrupting all that is sweet and scrumptious. Like most bakers, each hag cultivates a personal collection of favorite recipes they keep coming back to. For Larmine, the hag occupying Dalmira's Bakery, the most loyal of her specialties are her sticky toffee hounds.

Though modeled after noble hunting hounds, there's only so much magic can do to hold sponge cake and toffee sauce in a roughly canine shape. These sticky-sweet creations therefore have all the loyalty of a dog and all the versatility of an ooze, to the point that they practically hold themselves together through sheer force of devotion to their creator. However, the saccharine hounds have little awareness of their creator's mortality; were Larmine ever to die, Grayce would be serenaded nightly for weeks by the burbling howls of her mourning pets. In fact, the toffee oozes might eventually become so desperate for attention that they latch onto defenseless civilians, even suffocating their new (and unwitting) owners in a desperate quest for affection.

A sticky toffee hound is an irresistible trap for insects, whose congregation can give away the ooze's presence. The hound's body is ultimately lethal, though, trapping animals in its gooey hide like mosquitoes in amber.

Half Baked Creations

Sticky toffee hounds aren't the only option for enterprising sweet hags who want to make companions. Creatures like this can be in any form and shape, but animal shapes and behaviors are the most often mimicked. Sweet hags can also make companions out of breads, doughs, and other confections, lending to a buffet of dangerous and potentially tasty allies.

Sticky Paws.name: Sticky Paws
Sticky Paws.description: A sweet residue cakes the tracks left by a sticky toffee hound. A creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EA5vuSgJfiHH7plD]{Tracking} the hound can roll a [[/act track skill=cooking-lore]]{Cooking Lore} or [[/act track skill=crafting]]{Crafting} check instead of a Survival check. The creature can apply any modifiers to this check that involve identifying or preparing food, such as those granted by the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.1Eceqc6zbMj2x0q9]{Seasoned} skill feat or the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.fOIUmDGa9gkeCHA0]{Supertaster} general feat.

Motion Sense.name: Motion Sense
Motion Sense.description: A sticky toffee hound can sense nearby creatures through vibration and air movement.

Water Soluble.name: Water Soluble
Water Soluble.description: When exposed to at least 1 bulk of water, or a spell or effect with the water trait (even one that normally doesn't do any damage), the sticky toffee hound takes @Damage[10[acid]] damage as the sugar that makes up their body melts away, in addition to any damage that would normally be applied.

Overcooked.name: Overcooked
Overcooked.description:
Trigger The sticky toffee hound is reduced to 0 hit points by any method other than its water soluble weakness

Effect The sticky toffee hound explodes, dealing @Damage[1d4[bludgeoning],1d4[fire]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:15] with a @Check[reflex|dc:15|basic|options:area-effect] save.

Toffee Sauce.name: Toffee Sauce
Toffee Sauce.description: A creature hit by the sticky toffee hound's headbutt Strike is splattered by the sticky toffee sauce that soaks the creature's body, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} until the end of their next turn. On a critical hit, the creature instead becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2}.

Haunted Doll Cabinet.name: Haunted Doll Cabinet
Haunted Doll Cabinet.disable: @Check[occultism|dc:16] (trained) or @Check[religion|dc:16] (trained) to calm the spirits of one of three shelves in the cabinet
Haunted Doll Cabinet.hazarddescription: Three shelves inside a dusty cabinet each hold a row of dolls infused with the Doll House's malevolent spiritual energy.
Haunted Doll Cabinet.reset: The haunt deactivates 1 minute after all living creatures have left the area or when the soulbound dolls in the northwestern cabinet are destroyed. After 1 hour, the haunt is ready to trigger again. Putting Thalleus's spirit to rest permanently destroys the haunt.
Haunted Doll Cabinet.routine: (3 actions) For each shelf that remains, the haunt takes 1 action to target a living, non-construct creature in the room. Phantom dolls escape from the cabinet to rush that creature, clamber over them, and punch, kick, and bite them. The target takes @Damage[(1d6+2)[spirit]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:17|basic] save).

On Display.name: On Display
On Display.description:
Trigger At least two living creatures are in the room for more than a minute

Effect The dolls in the cabinet begin to shake and shudder, filling the area with a feeling of overwhelming dread about what might happen next. Each living creature who can see the cabinet must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:20|options:inflicts:frightened] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative.

Cruel Automatic Butler.name: Cruel Automatic Butler
Cruel Automatic Butler.publicNotes:
An automatic butler is a magical construct shaped like a wooden humanoid mannequin, usually tailored in a simple black suit and tie. It has only the barest hint of a face on its round head, though its jaw opens on a hinge to simulate regular mouth movements when it speaks. Its voice is often calm and measured, and it speaks quite politely. It follows the orders given to it by its creator (or anyone whom the creator has given permission to issue commands), which usually involves fetching items, keeping a room tidy, or ushering out guests. If unwanted guests become belligerent, an automatic butler can defend itself by battering intruders or using its innate magic to hurl objects with deadly force. Once a fight has ended, an automatic butler usually spends the next hour or so cleaning up the mess left behind. Automatic butlers are built on designs similar to soulbound dolls. Like other soulbound constructs, an automatic butler is animated by a fragment of the soul of a deceased mortal. This fragment can come from either a willing donor or an unwilling victim, who can resist the process with a successful Will save against the creator's Crafting DC. While resisting ruins the construct, the soul extraction process is often fatal, and the person dies regardless. Unlike with other soulbound constructs, the personality of the soul used to create an automatic butler is wholly suppressed. Instead, the automatic butler comports itself in the way a stereotypical servant would. Some automatic butlers are created with slightly different skill sets. They can be created to speak more languages beyond that of their creator, making them passable family diplomats who might welcome foreign guests. Some are trained to take care of tasks that require specialization, such as tutoring the youth of the household or tailoring the family's clothes. The sidebar covers some other options for a whole domestic staff of constructed servants.

Automatic Cooks and Gardeners

Should the designs for creating automatic butlers reach the wider world, someone would likely end up creating variations of the magical construct. These creatures would use the same basic statistics as an automatic butler, with a few minor changes. An automatic cook might have cleanse cuisine as an innate spell, a knife Strike, and the ability to shoot a jet of boiling hot water. An automatic gardener might have scatter scree and other spells with the earth or plant traits as innate spells, a hoe or shovel Strike, and the ability to pelt foes at range with seeds.
Cruel Automatic Butler.languagesDetails: one spoken by its creator (typically Common)

Mending.name: Mending
Mending.description:
You repair the target item. You restore 5 Hit Points per spell rank to the target, potentially removing the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6dNUvdb1dhToNDj3]{Broken} condition if this repairs it past the item's Broken Threshold. You can't replace lost pieces or repair an object that's been completely destroyed.

Heightened (2nd) You can target a non-magical object of 1 Bulk or less.

Heightened (3rd) You can target a non-magical object of 2 Bulk or less, or a magical object of 1 Bulk or less.

Cruel Bash.name: Cruel Bash
Cruel Bash.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The automatic butler makes a fist Strike. If it hits, it deals an additional 2d6 bludgeoning damage. This counts as two attacks for the automatic butler's multiple attack penalty.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

Soul Fragment.name: Soul Fragment
Soul Fragment.description: Like other soulbound constructs, an automatic butler is animated by soul energy, though the donor soul's personality is suppressed in favor of a simple demeanor, either politely helpful or stoically pragmatic. It also has none of that creature's memories. This soul fragment removes the immunity to spirit most constructs have, but because the automatic butler's personality overrides that of the original creature, the butler does have some resistance to spirit damage.

Telekinetic Hand.name: Telekinetic Hand
Telekinetic Hand.description:
You create a floating, magical hand, either invisible or ghostlike, that grasps the target object and levitates it slowly up to 20 feet in any direction. When you Sustain the spell, you can move the object an additional 20 feet. If the object is in the air when the spell ends, the object falls.

Heightened (3rd) You can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (7th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 2 or less.

Telekinetic Projectile.name: Telekinetic Projectile
Telekinetic Projectile.description:
You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

Alarm.name: Alarm
Alarm.description:
You ward an area to alert you when creatures enter without your permission. When you cast alarm, select a password. Whenever a Small or larger corporeal creature enters the spell's area without speaking the password, alarm sends your choice of a mental alert (in which case the spell gains the mental trait) or an audible alarm with the sound and volume of a hand bell (in which case the spell gains the auditory trait). Either option automatically awakens you, and the bell allows each creature in the area to attempt a @Check[perception|dc:15] check to wake up. A creature aware of the alarm must succeed at a Stealth check against the spell's DC or trigger the spell when moving into the area.

Heightened (3rd) You can specify a trigger for which types of creatures sound the alarm spell.

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

Right This Way.name: Right This Way
Right This Way.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The automatic butler attempts to usher a creature along while removing their coat. The automatic butler attempts an Athletics check to [[/act reposition]] a Large or smaller creature within reach. On a success, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} on a critical success) as the automatic butler pulls at some part of their clothing or gear. The target can remove this condition by taking an Interact action.

Final Blasphemy.name: Final Blasphemy
Final Blasphemy.description:
When the herexen is destroyed, it explodes in a wave of void energy with the effects of a 3-action @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.wdA52JJnsuQWeyqz]{Harm} spell (@Check[fortitude|dc:22]).

The herexen is destroyed, so it doesn't gain any Hit Points from this use of harm, and it doesn't need to have any harm spells remaining to use this ability

Harm.name: Harm
Harm.description:
You channel void energy to harm the living or heal the undead. If the target is a living creature, you deal 1d8 void damage to it, and it gets a basic Fortitude save. If the target is a willing undead creature, you restore that amount of Hit Points. The number of actions you spend when Casting this Spell determines its targets, range, area, and other parameters.

1 The spell has a range of touch.

2 (concentrate) The spell has a range of 30 feet. If you're healing an undead creature, increase the Hit Points restored by 8.

3 (concentrate) You disperse void energy in a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. This targets all living and undead creatures in the area.

Heightened (+1) The amount of healing or damage increases by 1d8, and the extra healing for the 2-action version increases by 8.

Longsword.name: Longsword
Longsword.description: Longswords, also known as arming swords, can be one-edged or two-edged swords. Their blades are heavy and they're between 3 and 4 feet in length.

Weapon Surge.name: Weapon Surge
Weapon Surge.description:
Holding your weapon aloft, you fill it with divine energy. On your next Strike with that weapon before the start of your next turn, you gain a +1 status bonus to the attack roll and the weapon deals an additional 1d6 spirit damage, and the Strike gains the sanctified trait. Weapon surge ends once you complete this Strike or the weapon leaves your possession.

Heightened (5th) The attack deals 2d6 additional spirit damage.

Heightened (9th) The attack deals 3d6 additional spirit damage.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.qlz0sJIvqc0FdUdr]{Spell Effect: Weapon Surge}

Heretic's Smite.name: Heretic's Smite
Heretic's Smite.description: While wielding a longsword, Genevye's Strikes deal an additional @Damage[1d6[spirit]] damage to creatures with the holy trait.

Trial by Poison Trap.name: Trial by Poison Trap
Trial by Poison Trap.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:23] (trained) to disable the launcher or @Check[arcana|dc:26] (expert) or @Check[occultism|dc:26] (expert) to disable the nearby magical sensor
Trial by Poison Trap.hazarddescription: A dart launcher embedded in the ceiling holds a cartridge of darts tipped with deadly poison.
Trial by Poison Trap.reset: The trap resets when an operator at the maze console in area A13 pulls the associated lever. The trap can be reset only once per minute.

Toxic Barrage.name: Toxic Barrage
Toxic Barrage.description:
Trigger An operator at the maze console in area A13 pulls the associated lever

Effect A dart launcher emerges from the ceiling and makes a poison dart Strike against two different creatures in the area marked on the map. A single creature can't be targeted more than once.

Unstable Floor.name: Unstable Floor
Unstable Floor.disable: @Check[engineering-lore|dc:20], @Check[mining-lore|dc:20], or @Check[survival|dc:23] to determine the exact extent of the unstable ground and to optionally cause it to collapse safely into area A2 below
Unstable Floor.hazarddescription: An unstable section of limestone crumbles under the weight of anyone who steps on it.

Deeper into the Darkness.name: Deeper into the Darkness
Deeper into the Darkness.description:
Trigger A Small or larger creature walks onto the weak limestone

Effect The ground collapses, and the triggering creature falls 15 feet into area A2 below. The creature can try to [[/act grab-an-edge dc=23]] to avoid falling, otherwise the fall inflicts @Damage[7[bludgeoning]] damage plus an additional @Damage[(4d6+3)[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:23|basic] save) from falling rubble.

Spitting Hot Candy Pot.name: Spitting Hot Candy Pot
Spitting Hot Candy Pot.disable: Breaking the pot disables it as soon as its rupture reaction is resolved.
Spitting Hot Candy Pot.hazarddescription: A massive bronze cauldron of molten candy bubbles on the stove, spraying sticky-sweet hot caramel in all directions.
Spitting Hot Candy Pot.routine:
(2 actions) On each of the pot's actions, it targets one creature hostile against Larmine within 30 feet of the pot, spitting a glob of hot molten candy that deals @Damage[(1d8+4)[fire]] damage; the target creature must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:16|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:slowed] save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage.

Failure The target takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} as the sticky molten candy glues them to the floor.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage, is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2}, and takes @Damage[1d4[persistent,fire]] damage as the hot candy sticks to their exposed skin.

Rupture.name: Rupture
Rupture.description:
Trigger The spitting hot candy pot Breaks

Effect The pot splits open, spilling its remaining contents in a @Template[type:cone|distance:15] that deals @Damage[2d12[fire]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:20|options:area-effect,damaging-effect] save. The area covered by this reaction lingers as difficult terrain for the rest of the encounter.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and becomes tangled in the sticky mess of hot candy, which imposes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds until it leaves the area of the rupture's effect. Until the creature leaves the area of effect, it also takes @Damage[1d4[persistent,fire]|options:area-damage] damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} (DC 18 to [[/act escape dc=18]]), after which it takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds and @Damage[1d4[persistent,fire]|options:area-damage] damage as failure.

Bubble Bubble.name: Bubble Bubble
Bubble Bubble.description:
Trigger Larmine rolls initiative

Effect With a wave of her hand, Larmine instantly brings her candy pot to a violent boil. The pot blows its top and targets all creatures hostile to Larmine within 20 feet of it, dealing @Damage[2d8[fire]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:16|basic|options:area-effect] save. On a critical failure, the targeted creature also takes @Damage[1d4[persistent,fire]|options:area-damage] damage as the hot candy sticks to their exposed skin. The spitting hot candy pot then rolls initiative.

Collapsing Ceiling.name: Collapsing Ceiling
Collapsing Ceiling.disable: @Check[crafting|dc:21] (trained) to support the damaged area against a collapse
Collapsing Ceiling.hazarddescription: A 5-foot-square section in the ceiling is in danger of collapsing. A character can use a Crafting check instead of a Perception check to detect the hazard.

Falling Rocks.name: Falling Rocks
Falling Rocks.description:
Trigger A creature enters a square where the ceiling's structure is weakened

Effect Rocks fall in the square, dealing @Damage[(4d8+10)[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:25|basic|options:area-effect] save) to anyone in that square. The square also turns into greater difficult terrain.

Leather Armor.name: Leather Armor
Leather Armor.description: A mix of flexible and molded boiled leather, a suit of this type of armor provides some protection with maximum flexibility.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: The Shiverscale kobold deals an extra 1d4 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Shortsword.name: Shortsword
Shortsword.description: These blades come in a variety of shapes and styles, but they are typically 2 feet long.

Scamper.name: Scamper
Scamper.description:
Requirements The kobold warrior is adjacent to at least one enemy

Effect The kobold warrior Strides up to their Speed plus 5 feet and gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against reactions triggered by this movement. They must end this movement in a space that's not adjacent to any enemy.

Crossbow (sypc).name: Crossbow
Crossbow (sypc).description: This ranged weapon has a bow-like assembly mounted on a handled frame called a tiller. The tiller has a mechanism to lock the bowstring in place, attached to a trigger mechanism that releases the tension and launches a bolt.

Greataxe.name: Greataxe
Greataxe.description: This large battle axe is too heavy to wield with only one hand. Many greataxes incorporate two blades, and they are often "bearded," having a hook at the bottom to increase the strength of their chopping power.

Leather Armor.name: Leather Armor
Leather Armor.description: A mix of flexible and molded boiled leather, a suit of this type of armor provides some protection with maximum flexibility.

Gummy Hands.name: Gummy Hands
Gummy Hands.description: Candies' residue gives Aezar an especially strong grip on her greataxe, which grants her a +2 circumstance bonus to her Reflex DC against attempts to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm} her.

Glutton's Rush.name: Glutton's Rush
Glutton's Rush.description: Aezar Strides twice and makes a jaws Strike. If she damages a living creature with this Strike, the temporary Hit Points she receives from glutton's feast is increased to 2d6.

Tooth Decay.name: Tooth Decay
Tooth Decay.description:
Frequent candy consumption has worsened Aezar's already poor dental health. If she takes 10 or more bludgeoning damage from a single attack or effect, she must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:25] save.

Success Aezar yells in pain but is otherwise unaffected.

Failure Several of Aezar's teeth break. She takes a –2 penalty to damage with her jaws Strike as well as to Athletics checks made as part of her @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.Tkd8sH4pwFIPzqTr]{Grab} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.uJSseLa57HZYSMUu]{Swallow Whole} abilities. These penalties last until Aezar is restored to her Hit Point maximum.

Critical Failure As failure, but so many of Aezar's teeth break that the penalty increases to –3 and she takes @Damage[(1d6-2)[persistent,bleed]] damage.

Glutton's Feast.name: Glutton's Feast
Glutton's Feast.description:
If Aezar damages a living creature with her jaws Strike, she gains 1d6 temporary Hit Points for 1 minute

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.LWFDNwi3iJuf476A]{Effect: Glutton's Feast (Aezar)}

Sticky Axe.name: Sticky Axe
Sticky Axe.description:
Trigger Aezar succeeds at a greataxe Strike against a creature

Effect Aezar's axe has a lingering residue from striking various sweets, and the sticky blade clings to her most recent victim, giving Aezar momentary leverage. Aezar can attempt to [[/act reposition]] or [[/act trip]] the target using the greataxe's reach, even though she doesn't have a free hand.

Alternatively, she can forgo either maneuver to drag the target toward her gaping mouth, granting her jaws unarmed Strike the agile trait for attacks made against the target until the end of her turn.

Spores.name: Spores
Spores.description: A creature that takes damage from a fungus leshy's spore pod Strike must attempt a saving throw with the same DC (@Check[fortitude|dc:16]) and effect as its Spore Cloud ability

Spore Cloud.name: Spore Cloud
Spore Cloud.description:
A fungus leshy can unleash a cloud of spores that irritates the eyes and throats of non-fungus creatures in a @Template[emanation|distance:15]. Each creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:16|options:area-effect,damaging-effect] save or take @Damage[1[persistent,poison]|options:area-damage] damage.

A creature has its vision reduced as long as the persistent damage continues and can see only within 20 feet.

Verdant Burst.name: Verdant Burst
Verdant Burst.description:
When a fungus leshy dies, a burst of primal energy explodes from its body, restoring @Damage[2d8[healing]] Hit Points to each fungi creature in a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. This area is filled with fungi, becoming difficult terrain.

If the terrain is not a viable environment for this fungi, they wither after 24 hours.

Speak with Plants (Constant, Fungi Only).name: Speak with Plants (Constant, Fungi Only)
Speak with Plants (Constant, Fungi Only).description:
You can ask questions of and receive answers from plants and fungi, but the spell doesn't make them more friendly or intelligent than normal. Most normal plants and fungi have a distinctive view of the world around them, so they don't recognize details about creatures or know anything about the world beyond their immediate vicinity. Cunning plant or fungus monsters are likely to be terse and evasive, while less intelligent ones often make inane comments.

Heightened (4th) The duration is 8 hours.

Change Shape.name: Change Shape
Change Shape.description:
The fungus leshy transforms into a giant mushroom or patch of fungi. This ability otherwise uses the effects of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.dileJ0Yxqg76LMvu]{One with Plants}.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

Balance Point.name: Balance Point
Balance Point.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:20] (trained) to attach the balanced stone floor piece to the actual floor and lock it in place, or @Check[crafting|dc:23] (trained) to jury-rig a quick bit of extra support to prevent the floor from tilting
Balance Point.hazarddescription: A 40-foot deep pit is obscured by a false floor set over a single balance point. Pressure on either side to the east or west causes occupants to fall into the depths below.

Tipping Floor.name: Tipping Floor
Tipping Floor.description:
Trigger A creature walks onto one side of the false floor

Effect The triggering creature falls into the pit and takes @Damage[20[bludgeoning]] damage from the fall unless they [[/act grab-an-edge dc=23]]. It's a @Check[athletics|dc:20] check to climb the pit walls.

Clothes Grab.name: Clothes Grab
Clothes Grab.description: A creature hit by the animated wardrobe's clothes whip becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} by the animated wardrobe. The creature isn't @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, but it can't move beyond the reach of the wardrobe's clothes whip. A creature can sever the clothes whip with a Strike against AC 15 that deals at least 5 slashing damage. This deals no damage to the animated wardrobe.

Construct Armor (Hardness 7).name: Construct Armor (Hardness  7)
Construct Armor (Hardness 7).description: Like normal objects, an animated wardrobe has Hardness. This Hardness reduces any damage it takes by an amount equal to the Hardness. Once an animated wardrobe is reduced to less than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon being damaged by a critical hit, its construct armor breaks, removing the Hardness and reducing its Armor Class to 17.

Enchanted Sweets.name: Enchanted Sweets
Enchanted Sweets.disable: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (3rd rank; counteract DC 20); destroying the case and its contents also shatters the enchantment and prevents further compulsion or poisonings.
Enchanted Sweets.hazarddescription: The enchanted pile of cookies and pastries arranged in this tasteful display case emit a supernaturally delicious aroma that compels those who fall under its smell to eat, eat, eat. No matter how many are consumed, the case always fills with more.
Enchanted Sweets.routine: (1 action) On the hazard's turn, if any creature is within the range of eatable enticement that is neither compelled by nor immune to it, the enchanted sweets target that creature with the same effect. Otherwise, it targets all creatures who have consumed some of its contents with a gut-rotting magical poison. Any creature who has consumed some of the enchanted sweets takes @Damage[2d12[poison]] damage with a @Check[fortitude|dc:22|basic] save.

Eatable Enticement.name: Eatable Enticement
Eatable Enticement.description:
Trigger A creature passes within 5 feet of the open northern side of the glass display case

Effect The tantalizing smell of the enchanted sweets overrides the target's olfactory senses. The target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24|options:inflicts:sickened] save. On a failure or critical failure, the enchanted sweets roll Initiative.

Critical Success The target is unaffected, immune to the enchanted sweets for 1 minute, and aware that the hazard was attempting to compel them.

Success The target is unaffected but remains unaware that the enchanted sweets were attempting to compel them.

Failure The target is compelled to remain beside the display case on its next turn and spend at least 2 of its actions consuming the enchanted sweets. It can repeat the Will save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. If compelled to consume the sweets for more than 2 consecutive rounds, the target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Critical Failure The target is compelled to spend all of its actions consuming the enchanted sweets and immediately becomes sickened 1. It can repeat the Will save at the end of each of its turns, ending the compulsion on a success.

The sickened condition increases by 1 for each turn the target is compelled to spend all of its actions consuming sweets, to a maximum of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 3}.

Wall Blades Trap.name: Wall Blades Trap
Wall Blades Trap.hp: to destroy the mechanisms in one wall
Wall Blades Trap.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:20] (trained) to disengage the mechanisms that operate the blades in one wall
Wall Blades Trap.hazarddescription: A series of rotating, serrated blades attached to long poles routinely slice out of grooves carved into the stone walls.
Wall Blades Trap.reset: The trap deactivates when the room is empty and resets after 1 minute.
Wall Blades Trap.routine: (3 actions) For each wall in which the mechanisms have been disabled or destroyed, the hazard has 1 fewer action. On each action, the hazard makes a serrated blade Strike against one creature within 10 feet of the west, east, or south wall. Each set of wall blades acts once per turn.

Slide and Dice.name: Slide and Dice
Slide and Dice.description:
Trigger A creature is within 10 feet of a trapped wall

Effect The hazard makes a serrated blade Strike against all creatures within 10 feet of the west, east, or south wall; these Strikes don't take a multiple attack penalty. The hazard then rolls initiative.

Unlucky Collapsing Tunnel.name: Unlucky Collapsing Tunnel
Unlucky Collapsing Tunnel.disable: @Check[nature|dc:18] check to counteract the aura of unluck that pervades the tunnels for 1 minute, or @Check[survival|dc:20] to support the tunnel ceiling properly without triggering a collapse
Unlucky Collapsing Tunnel.hazarddescription: At the unluckiest time, the shoddily supported tunnel wall collapses in on itself and floods the tunnel with dirt and stone.

Collapse.name: Collapse
Collapse.description:
Trigger A creature enters the tunnel

Effect The tunnel falls in, dealing @Damage[2d10[untyped]] damage to each creature in the area (@Check[reflex|dc:20|basic] save). Creatures in the area must spend at least 5 minutes digging themselves out to continue (@Check[survival|dc:20] halves this time).

Grasping Gems.name: Grasping Gems
Grasping Gems.disable: @Check[arcana|dc:22] (trained), @Check[occultism|dc:22] (trained), or @Check[nature|dc:22] (trained) to quiet one of the four grasping gems
Grasping Gems.hazarddescription: Four magically treated gems used to store fragments of souls begin glowing with an eerie malevolence.
Grasping Gems.reset: The haunt deactivates 1 minute after all living creatures have left the room. One hour after this or being Disabled, the haunt is ready to trigger again. Putting Thalleus's spirit to rest permanently destroys the haunt.
Grasping Gems.routine: (2 actions) During the haunt's first action, the grasping gems attempt an Athletics check (at a [[/r 1d20+4#Athletics]]{+14 modifier}) to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.PMbdMWc2QroouFGD]{Grapple} each non-@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} living creature in the room, rolling once and comparing the result to each target's Fortitude DC. For every gem that is disabled or destroyed, the haunt takes a cumulative –1 circumstance penalty to the check. For the haunt's second action, the gems' ghostly hands squeeze their victims. Each creature immobilized by the haunt takes @Damage[(2d8+5)[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:21|basic] save).

Phantom Hands.name: Phantom Hands
Phantom Hands.description:
Trigger A living creature is adjacent to a grasping gem's shelf

Effect The room becomes awash with eerie light as ghostly hands reach out from all directions. Each living creature in the room must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:24|options:area-effect,inflicts:immobilized] save. The haunt then rolls initiative.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The phantom hands interfere with the creature's movements. The creature takes a –2 status penalty to its initiative roll.

Failure The phantom hands hold the creature in place. The creature takes a –2 status penalty to its initiative roll and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} ([[/act escape dc=24]]) for the first round.

Critical Failure As failure, but if the creature attempts to Escape during the first round, it must roll twice and take the worse result. This is a misfortune effect.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.aBtlxHM9ChGywyrH]{Effect: Phantom Hands}

Studious Butler.name: Studious Butler
Studious Butler.publicNotes:
An automatic butler is a magical construct shaped like a wooden humanoid mannequin, usually tailored in a simple black suit and tie. It has only the barest hint of a face on its round head, though its jaw opens on a hinge to simulate regular mouth movements when it speaks. Its voice is often calm and measured, and it speaks quite politely. It follows the orders given to it by its creator (or anyone whom the creator has given permission to issue commands), which usually involves fetching items, keeping a room tidy, or ushering out guests. If unwanted guests become belligerent, an automatic butler can defend itself by battering intruders or using its innate magic to hurl objects with deadly force. Once a fight has ended, an automatic butler usually spends the next hour or so cleaning up the mess left behind. Automatic butlers are built on designs similar to soulbound dolls. Like other soulbound constructs, an automatic butler is animated by a fragment of the soul of a deceased mortal. This fragment can come from either a willing donor or an unwilling victim, who can resist the process with a successful Will save against the creator's Crafting DC. While resisting ruins the construct, the soul extraction process is often fatal, and the person dies regardless. Unlike with other soulbound constructs, the personality of the soul used to create an automatic butler is wholly suppressed. Instead, the automatic butler comports itself in the way a stereotypical servant would. Some automatic butlers are created with slightly different skill sets. They can be created to speak more languages beyond that of their creator, making them passable family diplomats who might welcome foreign guests. Some are trained to take care of tasks that require specialization, such as tutoring the youth of the household or tailoring the family's clothes. The sidebar covers some other options for a whole domestic staff of constructed servants.

Automatic Cooks and Gardeners

Should the designs for creating automatic butlers reach the wider world, someone would likely end up creating variations of the magical construct. These creatures would use the same basic statistics as an automatic butler, with a few minor changes. An automatic cook might have cleanse cuisine as an innate spell, a knife Strike, and the ability to shoot a jet of boiling hot water. An automatic gardener might have scatter scree and other spells with the earth or plant traits as innate spells, a hoe or shovel Strike, and the ability to pelt foes at range with seeds.
Studious Butler.languagesDetails: one spoken by its creator (typically Common)

Mending.name: Mending
Mending.description:
You repair the target item. You restore 5 Hit Points per spell rank to the target, potentially removing the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6dNUvdb1dhToNDj3]{Broken} condition if this repairs it past the item's Broken Threshold. You can't replace lost pieces or repair an object that's been completely destroyed.

Heightened (2nd) You can target a non-magical object of 1 Bulk or less.

Heightened (3rd) You can target a non-magical object of 2 Bulk or less, or a magical object of 1 Bulk or less.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

Soul Fragment.name: Soul Fragment
Soul Fragment.description: Like other soulbound constructs, an automatic butler is animated by soul energy, though the donor soul's personality is suppressed in favor of a simple demeanor, either politely helpful or stoically pragmatic. It also has none of that creature's memories. This soul fragment removes the immunity to spirit most constructs have, but because the automatic butler's personality overrides that of the original creature, the butler does have some resistance to spirit damage.

Telekinetic Hand.name: Telekinetic Hand
Telekinetic Hand.description:
You create a floating, magical hand, either invisible or ghostlike, that grasps the target object and levitates it slowly up to 20 feet in any direction. When you Sustain the spell, you can move the object an additional 20 feet. If the object is in the air when the spell ends, the object falls.

Heightened (3rd) You can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (7th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 2 or less.

Telekinetic Projectile.name: Telekinetic Projectile
Telekinetic Projectile.description:
You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

Alarm.name: Alarm
Alarm.description:
You ward an area to alert you when creatures enter without your permission. When you cast alarm, select a password. Whenever a Small or larger corporeal creature enters the spell's area without speaking the password, alarm sends your choice of a mental alert (in which case the spell gains the mental trait) or an audible alarm with the sound and volume of a hand bell (in which case the spell gains the auditory trait). Either option automatically awakens you, and the bell allows each creature in the area to attempt a @Check[perception|dc:15] check to wake up. A creature aware of the alarm must succeed at a Stealth check against the spell's DC or trigger the spell when moving into the area.

Heightened (3rd) You can specify a trigger for which types of creatures sound the alarm spell.

Studious Strike.name: Studious Strike
Studious Strike.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The automatic butler learns from its mistakes. If the butler's last action was to attempt a fist Strike that missed (but not critically missed) its target, the butler makes a fist Strike against the same target. The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to the attack, and on a hit, the butler deals an additional 1d6 precision damage.

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

Right This Way.name: Right This Way
Right This Way.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The automatic butler attempts to usher a creature along while removing their coat. The automatic butler attempts an Athletics check to [[/act reposition]] a Large or smaller creature within reach. On a success, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} on a critical success) as the automatic butler pulls at some part of their clothing or gear. The target can remove this condition by taking an Interact action.

Cursed Digging Machine.name: Cursed Digging Machine
Cursed Digging Machine.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:18] (trained) twice on the cart to dismantle core connected pieces, or @Check[nature|dc:20] or @Check[occultism|dc:20] (trained) check to temporarily disable the jinkins' curse and render the machine inert for an hour
Cursed Digging Machine.hazarddescription: A large, wheeled cart with a multi-sectioned pole in the middle. Each section of pole has several shovels sticking out of it like makeshift arms.
Cursed Digging Machine.routine: (3 actions) The digging machine spends an action to move 20 feet toward the nearest creature. If it starts next to a creature, it moves 20 feet toward the next closest creature. It then makes two slashing shovels attacks against any creature within 10 feet.

Crash and Slash.name: Crash and Slash
Crash and Slash.description:
Trigger A creature comes within 30 feet of the digging machine

Effect The digging machine rattles to life and rolls toward the triggering creature. It moves 30 feet toward the creature, attacking every creature within 10 feet with slashing shovels. The machine then rolls initiative.

Consume Flesh.name: Consume Flesh
Consume Flesh.description:
Requirements The ghoul is adjacent to the corpse of a creature that died within the last hour.

Effect The ghoul devours a chunk of the corpse and regains @Damage[(1+(max(0,floor(@actor.level/2))))d6[healing]] Hit Points.

It can regain Hit Points from any given corpse only once.

Frightful Snarl.name: Frightful Snarl
Frightful Snarl.description: Krethark snarls and glares at a creature within 30 feet that he can see, and then attempts to [[/act demoralize]] that creature; he doesn't take a penalty if the creature doesn't understand his language. A creature that becomes frightened by Frightful Snarl is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the start of their turn.

Grave Knowledge.name: Grave Knowledge
Grave Knowledge.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The ghoul calls upon knowledge it retains from one creature it has consumed in the past 7 days. The ghoul attempts a skill check using a skill in which the consumed creature was trained (if it's unclear whether the creature was trained, the GM decides). The ghoul is treated as trained and uses the high skill modifier for the ghoul's level ([[/gmr 1d20+12]]). This takes the same amount of actions or time as usual for the check.

The ghoul can instead automatically learn something specific known by a creature it consumed in the last 7 days, like the location of a hidden treasure or the name of a loved one. The ghoul can do this only once for a given creature, no matter how much of its flesh the ghoul consumed.

Swift Leap.name: Swift Leap
Swift Leap.description: The ghoul jumps up to half its Speed. This movement doesn't trigger reactions.

Breastplate.name: Breastplate
Breastplate.description: Though referred to as a breastplate, this type of armor consists of several pieces of plate or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.pRoikbRo5HFW6YUB]{Half Plate} armor that protect the torso, chest, neck, and sometimes the hips and lower legs. It strategically grants some of the protection of plate while allowing greater flexibility and speed.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: Krethark deals 1d6 extra precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Inheritor's Kiss (eEpi).name: Inheritor's Kiss
Inheritor's Kiss (eEpi).description: This broad-bladed sword, sometimes called the hand-and-a-half sword, has a longer grip so it can be held in one hand or used with two hands to provide extra slashing power.

Ghoul Whispers.name: Ghoul Whispers
Ghoul Whispers.description:
Requirements A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} creature is within the ghoul's reach

Effect The ghoul whispers dark thoughts and vile cravings into the creature's ears. The creature must save against the forbidden cravings curse.

Forbidden Cravings (curse) A creature can still eat and drink while sickened by this curse

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:21|traits:curse], using the high spell DC for the ghoul's level

Stage 1 carrier with no ill effects (1 day)

Stage 2 @Damage[2d6[void]] damage and the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} until it consumes raw meat (1 day)

Stage 3 as stage 2

Stage 4 as stage 2 unless the target has consumed raw meat in the past 24 hours, then it takes @Damage[4d6[void]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} until it consumes raw meat;

Stage 5 if the creature has eaten raw meat in the past 24 hours, it dies and rises as a ghoul, if not, it returns to stage 4

Telekinetic Maneuver.name: Telekinetic Maneuver
Telekinetic Maneuver.description: With a rush of telekinetic power, you move a foe or something they carry. You can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.7blmbDrQFNfdT731]{Shove}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.lOE4yjUnETTdaf2T]{Reposition}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ge56Lu1xXVFYUnLP]{Trip} the target using a spell attack roll instead of an Athletics check.

Staff.name: Staff
Staff.description: This long piece of wood can aid in walking and deliver a mighty blow.

Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
Detect Magic.description:
You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an invisibility potion) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

Daze.name: Daze
Daze.description:
You push into the target's mind and daze it with a mental jolt. The jolt deals 1d6 mental damage, with a basic Will save. If the target critically fails the save, it is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

Ill Omen.name: Ill Omen
Ill Omen.description:
The target is struck with misfortune, which throws it off balance. The target must attempt a Will save.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The first time during the duration that the target attempts an attack roll or skill check, it must roll twice and use the worse result.

Critical Failure Every time during the duration that the target attempts an attack roll or skill check, it must roll twice and use the worse result.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.AmsVO5Q6078mEvNt]{Spell Effect: Ill Omen}

Leather Armor.name: Leather Armor
Leather Armor.description: A mix of flexible and molded boiled leather, a suit of this type of armor provides some protection with maximum flexibility.

Telekinetic Projectile.name: Telekinetic Projectile
Telekinetic Projectile.description:
You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

Fear.name: Fear
Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

Bane.name: Bane
Bane.description:
You fill the minds of your enemies with doubt. Enemies in the area must succeed at a Will save or take a –1 status penalty to attack rolls as long as they are in the area. Once per round on subsequent turns, you can Sustain the spell to increase the emanation's radius by 10 feet and force enemies in the area that weren't yet affected to attempt another saving throw.

Bane can counteract @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.XSujb7EsSwKl19Uu]{Bless}.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.UTLp7omqsiC36bso]{Spell Effect: Bane}

Force Barrage.name: Force Barrage
Force Barrage.description:
You fire a shard of solidified magic toward a creature that you can see. It automatically hits and deals 1d4+1 force damage. For each additional action you use when Casting the Spell, increase the number of shards you shoot by one, to a maximum of three shards for 3 actions. You choose the target for each shard individually. If you shoot more than one shard at the same target, combine the damage before applying bonuses or penalties to damage, resistances, weaknesses, and so forth.

Heightened (+2) You fire one additional shard with each action you spend.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

Stupefy.name: Stupefy
Stupefy.description:
You dull the target's mind, depending on its Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} until the start of your next turn.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 3} for 1 minute.

Dagger (b8VS).name: Dagger
Dagger (b8VS).description: This small, bladed weapon is held in one hand and used to stab a creature in close combat. It can also be thrown.

Shield.name: Shield
Shield.description:
You raise a magical shield of force. This counts as using the Raise a Shield action, giving you a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn, but it doesn't require a hand to use.

While the spell is in effect, you can use the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.jM72TjJ965jocBV8]{Shield Block} reaction with your magic shield. The shield has Hardness 5. You can use the spell's reaction to reduce damage from any spell or magical effect, even if it doesn't deal physical damage. After you use Shield Block, the spell ends and you can't cast it again for 10 minutes.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.Jemq5UknGdMO7b73]{Spell Effect: Shield}

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.QF6RDlCoTvkVHRo4]{Effect: Shield Immunity}

Heightened (+2) The shield's Hardness increases by 5.

Blood Vendetta.name: Blood Vendetta
Blood Vendetta.description:
Requirements You can bleed.

Trigger A creature deals piercing, slashing, or persistent bleed damage to you.

You curse the target, punishing it for having the audacity to spill your blood. The target takes 2d6 persistent bleed damage and must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half the persistent bleed damage.

Failure The target takes the full persistent bleed damage. Until the bleeding stops, the target has weakness 1 to piercing and slashing damage. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.buXx8Azr4BYWPtFg]{Spell Effect: Blood Vendetta (Failure)}

Critical Failure As failure, but the target takes double the persistent bleed damage.

Heightened (+2) The persistent bleed damage increases by 2d6.

Acid Spray Trap.name: Acid Spray Trap
Acid Spray Trap.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:20] (trained) to disable one of the two acid-spewing nozzles or @Check[crafting|dc:21] (trained) to rig a makeshift plug for one of the two nozzles
Acid Spray Trap.hazarddescription: Hidden nozzles in the ceiling spray acid pumped in from a nearby reservoir to destroy the desk and all its documents, as well as anyone trying to retrieve those documents.
Acid Spray Trap.reset: The trap deactivates after 1 minute. To be reset, the trap's reserve tanks must be refilled with acid.
Acid Spray Trap.routine: (1 action) The nozzles spray acid from the ceiling onto every creature adjacent to the desk. Each affected creature takes @Damage[4d6[acid]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:20|basic|options:area-effect] save). For each broken nozzle, this damage is reduced by 2d6.

Ooze Surprise.name: Ooze Surprise
Ooze Surprise.description:
Trigger A creature flips the switches on the underside of the desk in the wrong order or a creature attempts to open one of the desk drawers without first disabling the trap

Effect A hatch opens in the ceiling, releasing a string slime onto the desk. The string slime makes a pseudopod Strike against one creature within reach before rolling initiative. The trap then rolls initiative.

Spiked Walls.name: Spiked Walls
Spiked Walls.disable: [[/act disable-device dc=15]]{Thievery} (trained) to snip the trip wire or jam the panel
Spiked Walls.hazarddescription: A low trip wire connects to a lattice panel covered with wooden spikes.

Spiked Wall.name: Spiked Wall
Spiked Wall.description:
Trigger A creature triggers the trip wire

Effect A lattice panel lashed with wooden spikes swings shut across the passage. The triggering creature takes @Damage[3d6[piercing]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:17|basic] save). The panel provides lesser @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.other-effects.Item.I9lfZUiCwMiGogVi]{Cover} and prevents movement along the passage. The panel can be pushed open like a door with an Interact action, but it swings shut again unless wedged open with a heavy object.

Automatic Butler.name: Automatic Butler
Automatic Butler.publicNotes:
An automatic butler is a magical construct shaped like a wooden humanoid mannequin, usually tailored in a simple black suit and tie. It has only the barest hint of a face on its round head, though its jaw opens on a hinge to simulate regular mouth movements when it speaks. Its voice is often calm and measured, and it speaks quite politely. It follows the orders given to it by its creator (or anyone whom the creator has given permission to issue commands), which usually involves fetching items, keeping a room tidy, or ushering out guests. If unwanted guests become belligerent, an automatic butler can defend itself by battering intruders or using its innate magic to hurl objects with deadly force. Once a fight has ended, an automatic butler usually spends the next hour or so cleaning up the mess left behind. Automatic butlers are built on designs similar to soulbound dolls. Like other soulbound constructs, an automatic butler is animated by a fragment of the soul of a deceased mortal. This fragment can come from either a willing donor or an unwilling victim, who can resist the process with a successful Will save against the creator's Crafting DC. While resisting ruins the construct, the soul extraction process is often fatal, and the person dies regardless. Unlike with other soulbound constructs, the personality of the soul used to create an automatic butler is wholly suppressed. Instead, the automatic butler comports itself in the way a stereotypical servant would. Some automatic butlers are created with slightly different skill sets. They can be created to speak more languages beyond that of their creator, making them passable family diplomats who might welcome foreign guests. Some are trained to take care of tasks that require specialization, such as tutoring the youth of the household or tailoring the family's clothes. The sidebar covers some other options for a whole domestic staff of constructed servants.

Automatic Cooks and Gardeners

Should the designs for creating automatic butlers reach the wider world, someone would likely end up creating variations of the magical construct. These creatures would use the same basic statistics as an automatic butler, with a few minor changes. An automatic cook might have cleanse cuisine as an innate spell, a knife Strike, and the ability to shoot a jet of boiling hot water. An automatic gardener might have scatter scree and other spells with the earth or plant traits as innate spells, a hoe or shovel Strike, and the ability to pelt foes at range with seeds.
Automatic Butler.languagesDetails: one spoken by its creator (typically Common)

Mending.name: Mending
Mending.description:
You repair the target item. You restore 5 Hit Points per spell rank to the target, potentially removing the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6dNUvdb1dhToNDj3]{Broken} condition if this repairs it past the item's Broken Threshold. Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

Soul Fragment.name: Soul Fragment
Soul Fragment.description: Like other soulbound constructs, an automatic butler is animated by soul energy, though the donor soul's personality is suppressed in favor of a simple demeanor, either politely helpful or stoically pragmatic. It also has none of that creature's memories. This soul fragment removes the immunity to spirit most constructs have, but because the automatic butler's personality overrides that of the original creature, the butler does have some resistance to spirit damage.

Telekinetic Hand.name: Telekinetic Hand
Telekinetic Hand.description:
You create a floating, magical hand, either invisible or ghostlike, that grasps the target object and levitates it slowly up to 20 feet in any direction. When you Sustain the spell, you can move the object an additional 20 feet. If the object is in the air when the spell ends, the object falls.

Heightened (3rd) You can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (7th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 2 or less.

Telekinetic Projectile.name: Telekinetic Projectile
Telekinetic Projectile.description:
You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

Alarm.name: Alarm
Alarm.description:
You ward an area to alert you when creatures enter without your permission. When you cast alarm, select a password. Whenever a Small or larger corporeal creature enters the spell's area without speaking the password, alarm sends your choice of a mental alert (in which case the spell gains the mental trait) or an audible alarm with the sound and volume of a hand bell (in which case the spell gains the auditory trait). Either option automatically awakens you, and the bell allows each creature in the area to attempt a @Check[perception|dc:15] check to wake up. A creature aware of the alarm must succeed at a Stealth check against the spell's DC or trigger the spell when moving into the area.

Heightened (3rd) You can specify a trigger for which types of creatures sound the alarm spell.

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

Right This Way.name: Right This Way
Right This Way.description:

Effect The automatic butler attempts to usher a creature along while removing their coat. The automatic butler attempts an Athletics check to [[/act reposition]] a Large or smaller creature within reach. On a success, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} on a critical success) as the automatic butler pulls at some part of their clothing or gear. The target can remove this condition by taking an Interact action.

Sangrist.name: Sangrist
Sangrist.publicNotes:
Sangrists are born from the bodies of those who bled out completely, often when they are left unburied without proper rites in places tainted by void energy, though the strong presence of void energy is not a requirement. Some victims who rise as sangrists suffered an accident or attack in a remote region and were never found and properly laid to rest, be it a slip of a blade when cleaning game or being gored by a wild hog.

After rising as undead, these tragic creatures are drawn to sites of past carnage where the scent of blood and death lingers. They are commonly found in the war-torn lands of Lastwall, the haunted ruins of Ustalav, and the cursed battlefields of Geb, embodying a relentless hunger for the life they lost.

Sangrists rely on stealth and ambushes, becoming more active at night. During times of inactivity, they fall into a strange stupor. In this state, they rock back and forth and frequently twitch, sometimes emitting a haunting humming sound.

Some sangrists are solitary hunters, often stalking a solitary target for hours if not days. Others form packs, especially if they shared a bond in life. These packs exhibit a chilling, coordinated cunning, reminiscent of wolves on the prowl. Sangrists are patient hunters, sometimes tracking their victims for miles or observing them for hours before making a move. They target the weak and isolated, picking off those they can easily wound so that they bleed out even if they manage to outrun the sangrists. Retaining only a shadow of their former selves, sangrists rarely utter more than single-word sentences, usually to express their hatred for the living, their unending hunger, or where victims can be found.

Although sangrists can't drink blood or gain nourishment from it, they sometimes pool blood in their cupped hands and pour it on their faces and bodies. They may also lie down next to the body of a slain enemy. This macabre ritual seems to be a desperate attempt to reconnect with the life they once had. These strange proclivities toward blood, nighttime activity, and the yearning for some semblance of their previous lives lead some sangrists to associate with vampires. Vampires generally don't find sangrists distasteful and find the undead creatures easy to manipulate into serving them as guardians and attendants.

Taste for Blood

These rare creatures have been mistaken for either feral vampires or blood obsessed zombies by soldiers and adventurers who don't have a firm understanding of the myriad forms undeath can come in. Those familiar with sangrists and who aim to hunt them often set out blood, frequently pig blood, as a lure.

Blood Vigor.name: Blood Vigor
Blood Vigor.description: While adjacent to a creature taking persistent bleed damage, the sangrist gains fast healing 3 and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} until the start of its next turn. The sangrist can use its extra action only to Step or Stride.

Bloodletter.name: Bloodletter
Bloodletter.description: A sangrist intuitively exacerbates open cuts on living creatures with its attacks. The sangrint's claw Strikes deal an additional 1 precision damage to living creatures taking persistent bleed damage.

Blood Scent.name: Blood Scent
Blood Scent.description: A sangrist can detect creatures taking persistent bleed damage as an imprecise sense at the listed range.

Gauntling.name: Gauntling
Gauntling.publicNotes:
In places like the Gravelands, undeath permeates the very soil of the land. This unholy pollution can have significant effects on regional flora and fauna over the course of generations, causing plants to become twisted and diseased looking and contaminates wildlife so their remains spontaneously rise as mindless undead.

Yet in some cases, particularly for those beasts who forage primarily through the act of scavenging, the consumption of undead flesh can have an entirely different effect over the course of months. How quickly an animal is affected depends on whether it ate from the remains of an undead creature left behind after its destruction or consumed it "fresh" from an undead in a desperate throe of starvation. Assuming the unfortunate creature survives any onset of disease or other afflictions brought on by their ghastly repast, these scavengers sometimes undergo a transformation into a twisted, ravenous beast known as a gauntling.

Most gauntlings arise from scavengers, carnivores, or omnivores, but in certain cases, desperate herbivores can become transformed as well—these creatures are perhaps the most disturbing type of gauntling, due to the significant change in their behaviors pushing them toward diets of fresh meat. Once animals become gauntlings, these creatures abandon their previous wilderness habitats in favor of those near more settled regions and often choose sewers or other underground locales as dens from which they emerge to hunt. In their transformation into a gauntling, regardless of what the creature's previous dietary leanings might have been, all gauntlings share one horrific hunger—the flesh of sapient humanoids. A gauntling looks similar to the animal it was before its transformation, but with large sharp fangs and with painfully emaciated frames, regardless of how much they eat.

This gauntling (as are all of those encountered in Troubles in Grayce) were once boars, but you can use these statistics to represent any terrestrial Medium animal that's succumbed to this unholy transformation. Regardless of its original form, all gauntlings share a mouthful of sharp, twisted fangs.

Other Gauntlings

The gauntling presented here comes from a Medium terrestrial animal (a boar, to be precise), but other animals can be transformed in this way by consuming undead flesh. To represent one from a swimming or flying Medium animal, simply grant it a swim or fly speed equal to its base speed. To represent a smaller or larger creature, use the statistics presented here as a starting point, then rebuild the statistics using the guidelines for building creatures that begin on page 112 of GM Core

Soul Ravage.name: Soul Ravage
Soul Ravage.description:
A gauntling's fangs carry with them a potent curse that eagerly seeps into living flesh. The first time in a round that a creature takes damage from a gauntling's jaws Strike, they must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:18|options:inflicts:sickened] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} and can't reduce its sickened value below 1 for 1 minute.

Critical Failure As failure, but for 1 hour. A creature that dies while under this curse's effects rises within 24 hours as a zombie.

Hot Oven.disable: 1 Interact action and a @Check[athletics|dc:18] check to close the oven door after it's been opened.
Hot Oven.hazarddescription: This fiery hot oven needs to be extra-large to keep up with the demands of the bakery—large enough for a Medium creature to crawl inside. Or be pushed.
Hot Oven.reset: The oven door can be opened and closed freely, as described above, for the course of the entire combat. If left to its own devices, the oven burns through its fuel and goes out roughly 1 hour after it's lit.

Hot to the Touch.description:
Trigger A creature attempts to open the closed oven door without the protection of an oven mitt

Effect The triggering creature takes @Damage[(1d10+3)[fire]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:22|basic] save).

In You Go!.name: In You Go!
In You Go!.description:
Trigger A creature moves or is forcibly moved into the open oven

Effect The triggering creature takes @Damage[3d10[fire]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:25|basic] save) and @Damage[2d6[persistent,fire]] damage. This damage repeats at the beginning of the creature's turn for as long as it remains inside the oven.

Goblin Scuttle.description:

Zini makes fun of either Aezar or Grizzle while she can observe them within 30 feet of her. She attempts a @Check[deception|against:will] check with a +2 circumstance bonus against the creature's Will DC. Zini cannot use this ability again against that creature until she spends at least 10 minutes thinking about a worthy second insult.

Critical Success As success, but the target also takes @Damage[(1d4+2)[mental]] damage.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} against the next attack an ally attempts against the target before the beginning of Zini's next turn.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: The jinkin deals 1d6 extra precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Dart.name: Dart

Requirements Alendreu is wielding an orc necksplitter in each hand

Effect Alendreu lashes out with both axes. He attempts two Strikes, one with each necksplitter, each using his current multiple attack penalty. Both Strikes must have the same target, and the second strike takes a –2 penalty.
